Reset the segment cache after segment initialization in vmx_vcpu_reset()
to harden KVM against caching stale/uninitialized data.  Without the
recent fix to bypass the cache in kvm_arch_vcpu_put()
scenario is possible:
- vCPU is just created
column2: and the vCPU thread is preempted before

column1: SS.AR_BYTES is written in vmx_vcpu_reset().
- When scheduling out the vCPU task
vmx_get_cpl() reads and caches '0' for SS.AR_BYTES.
- vmx_vcpu_reset() => seg_setup() configures SS.AR_BYTES
invoke vmx_segment_cache_clear() to invalidate the cache.
As a result
column2: KVM retains a stale value in the cache

column1: e.g. via KVM_GET_SREGS.  Usually this is not a problem because the VMX
segment cache is reset on each VM-Exit
column2: but if the userspace VMM (e.g KVM

column1: selftests) reads and writes system registers just after the vCPU was
created
stale '0' value and ultimately will trigger a VM-Entry failure due to
incorrect SS segment type.
Invalidating the cache after writing the VMCS doesn't address the general
issue of cache accesses from IRQ context being unsafe
KVM from clobbering the VMCS
